source.text: ወእምህየ፡ ሖርኩ፡ ካልአ፡ መካነ፡ ወአርአየኒ፡ በምዕራብ፡ *ደብረ፡ ዐቢየ፡ ወ*ነዋኅ፡ ወ*ኵኵሐ፡ ጽኑዐ።
source.note: Direct visual collation of the selected Charles1906 printed main text. Actual critical signs retained; only raised apparatus labels and printed verse labels suppressed. Punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial supplies and conjectures are not independent manuscript verification.

translation.text: From there I went to another place, and he showed me in the west a great, high mountain and solid rock.

source.text: ወአርባዕቱ፡ መካናት፡ †ሠናያት፡ [ወ]በውስቴቱ፡ ዘቦቱ፡ *ዕሙቀ፡ ወርኂበ፡ ወልሙጸ፡ ጥቀ፡ (ሠለስቱ፡ እምኔሆን፡ ጸልማት፡ ወአሐቲ፡ ብርህት፡ ወነቅዐ፡ ማይ፡ በማእከላ፡ እቤ፡) ከመ፡ ልሙጽ፡ †ዘያንኩረኵር፡† ወዕሙቅ፡ ወጽልመት፡ ለነጽሮ።
source.note: Direct visual collation of the selected Charles1906 printed main text. Actual critical signs retained; only raised apparatus labels and printed verse labels suppressed. Punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial supplies and conjectures are not independent manuscript verification. The leading dagger before ሠናያት has no printed closing partner; the two daggers around the rolling expression are retained. The entire parenthesis is editorial Greek-based supply, not merely punctuation.

translation.text: Within it were four places, “beautiful,” deep, wide, and very smooth.[a] (Three of them were dark and one bright, with a spring of water in its midst. I said:)[b] How smooth—rolling—and deep and dark to look at![c]

footnotes.text: The selected main text explicitly says four. Its daggered adjective ሠናያት means beautiful or fine (Dillmann1865 cols251–252), but Charles printed56 note12 regards it as corrupt and explains it through a Greek confusion involving hollows. This English retains the actual adjective in quotation marks rather than silently changing it to a hollow or compartment.

The parenthesized sentence, including I said, is printed in the selected main text but supplied by the editor from the Greek (Charles printed56 note15). Parentheses here preserve that editorial status; this is not an independently witnessed Ethiopic sentence.

The rolling expression is daggered as corrupt in the selected text (Charles printed56 note16). The root relates to rolling or causing to roll (Dillmann1865 col838, including Hen22:2); the short English rolling is only a qualified rendering of the damaged clause, not a restoration of its syntax or a claim that this means a cavern.

source.text: ውእቱ፡ ጊዜ፡ አውሥአ፡ ሩፋኤል፡ ፩*እምነ፡ ቅዱሳን፡ መላእክት፡ እንዘ፡ ሀለወ፡ ምስሌየ፡ ወይቤለኒ፡ ዝመካናት፡ †ሰናያት፡† ከመ፡ ይትጋብኡ፡ ዲቤሆን፡ *መናፍስት፡ ለነፍሶሙ፡ ለምዉታን፤ *ሎቱ፡ ዝንቱ፡ ተፈጥሩ፡ ዝየ፡ ያስተጋብኡ፡ ኵሎ፡ ነፍሰ፡ ውሉደ፡ ሰብእ።
source.note: Direct visual collation of the selected Charles1906 printed main text. Actual critical signs retained; only raised apparatus labels and printed verse labels suppressed. Punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial supplies and conjectures are not independent manuscript verification. Actual እንዘ read from the main-text image, not OCR እግዚ. Source terms መናፍስት and ነፍስ remain distinct in transcription without importing philosophical categories.

translation.text: Then Raphael, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered and said to me, “These ‘beautiful’ places are for the spirits of the souls of the dead to gather in. For this they were created: to gather here every soul of the children of humanity.”[a]

footnotes.text: The adjective is again daggered as corrupt; see22:2. The selected wording explicitly has spirits of their souls, of the dead, followed by every soul. These terms are retained without imposing a fixed philosophical distinction: Dillmann1865 cols707–709 shows overlapping life, soul and spirit uses and explicitly lists spirits of dead people with Hen22:3. The collection clause is syntactically awkward; for this supplies the sense of the printed literally for it, this.

source.text: ወእሙንቱ፡ መካናት፡ ኀበ፡ ይነብርዎሙ፡ †ገብሩ፡† እስከ፡ ዕለተ፡ ኵነኔሆሙ፡ ወእስከ፡ አመ፡ ዕድሜሆሙ፡ ወዕድሜ፡ [ውእቱ፡ ዘየዓቢ፡] *እስከ፡ አመ፡ ኵነኔ፡ ዐቢይ፡ በላዕሌሆሙ።
source.note: Direct visual collation of the selected Charles1906 printed main text. Actual critical signs retained; only raised apparatus labels and printed verse labels suppressed. Punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial supplies and conjectures are not independent manuscript verification.

translation.text: These places were made to keep them until the day of their judgment, until the time of their appointed term—the term [which is greater]—until the great judgment comes upon them.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected clause is damaged: the daggered ገብሩ is an active they made, not the passive were made used to give the place-clause a workable English construction. Charles printed56 note31 and printed57 note10 discuss the broken construction. The doubled term or duration and bracketed which is greater are retained, not silently replaced by a smooth determined-time formula. The verb comes in the last clause is supplied in English; the source has until the time of great judgment upon them.

source.text: ርኢኩ፡ *መናፍስተ፡ ውሉደ፡ ሰብእ፡ እንዘ፡ ሙታን፡ ውእቶሙ፡ ወቃሎሙ፡ ይበጽሕ፡ እስከ፡ ሰማይ፡ ወይስኪ።
source.note: Direct visual collation of the selected Charles1906 printed main text. Actual critical signs retained; only raised apparatus labels and printed verse labels suppressed. Punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial supplies and conjectures are not independent manuscript verification.

translation.text: I saw the spirits of the children of humanity who were dead. Their voice reached heaven and made accusation.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected Ethiopic has plural dead people and their voice, although the following question asks about a single spirit. This English does not silently adopt the singular reconstruction proposed in Charles printed57 note12. The accusation sense of ሰከየ is lexically supported by Dillmann1865 col383, which cites Hen22:5.

source.text: ውእቱ፡ ጊዜ፡ ተስእልክዎ፡ ለሩፋኤል፡ መልአክ፡ እንዘ፡ ሀሎ፡ ምስሌየ፡ ወእቤሎ፡ ዝመንፈስ፡ ዘመኑ፡ ውእቱ፡ ዘከመዝ፡ ቃሉ፡ ይበጽሕ፡ ወይሰኪ።
source.note: Direct visual collation of the selected Charles1906 printed main text. Actual critical signs retained; only raised apparatus labels and printed verse labels suppressed. Punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial supplies and conjectures are not independent manuscript verification. Complete unit crosses printed56→58/PDF94→96; PDF95 is facing Greek plus continuation apparatus, not a new Ethiopic unit.

translation.text: Then I asked Raphael, the angel who was with me, “Whose spirit is this, whose voice rises in this way and makes accusation?”

source.text: ወአውሥአኒ፡ [ወይቤለኒ፡] እንዘ፡ ይብል፡ ዝንቱ፡ መንፈስ፡ ውእቱ፡ ዘ*ወጽአ፡ እምአቤል፡ ዘ*ቀተሎ፡ ቃየን፡ እኁሁ፡ ወይሰኪ፡ ኪያሁ፡ እስከ፡ ሶበ፡ ይትኀጐል፡ ዘርኡ፡ እምቅድመ፡ *ገጸ፡ ለምድር፡ ወእምዘርአ፡ ሰብእ፡ ይማስን፡ ዘርኡ።
source.note: Direct visual collation of the selected Charles1906 printed main text. Actual critical signs retained; only raised apparatus labels and printed verse labels suppressed. Punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial supplies and conjectures are not independent manuscript verification.

translation.text: He answered me, saying, “This is the spirit that came out of Abel, whom his brother Cain killed. It accuses him until his offspring is destroyed from the face of the earth and his offspring disappears from the descendants of humanity.”[a]

footnotes.text: The selected text brackets and said to me as a doublet of saying (Charles printed58 note6); English represents the speech once. Abel is the source of the spirit, Cain the killer and target of its accusation; the repeated his offspring refers to Cain in this interpretation. Charles marks the came out wording as an emendation (printed58 note7); the chosen critical wording is retained without claiming independent manuscript confirmation.

source.text: ውእተ፡ ጊዜ፡ ተስእልኩ፡ [በእንቲአሁ፡ ወ]በእንተ፡ †ኵነኔ፡ †ኵሉ፡ በእንተ፡ ምንት፡ ተፈልጡ፡ ፩እምነ፡ ፩።
source.note: Direct visual collation of the selected Charles1906 printed main text. Actual critical signs retained; only raised apparatus labels and printed verse labels suppressed. Punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial supplies and conjectures are not independent manuscript verification. The printed † before each of ኵነኔ and ኵሉ is retained; no closing daggers invented.

translation.text: Then I asked [about him and] about all the judgment: “Why have they been separated from one another?”[a]

footnotes.text: Judgment is the selected daggered noun, followed by a daggered all; it is not a secure word for compartments. Charles printed58 notes18–20 treats the bracketed phrase as an intrusion and discusses corruption and word order. This English keeps the printed noun and marked bracketed addition, without silently adopting the editor’s explanation through Greek hollows. The objects of separated are not named again in this unit.

source.text: *ወአውሥአኒ፡ ወይቤለኒ፡ እሉ፡ ፫ትገብሩ፡ ከመ፡ ይትፈለጠ፡ መንፈሶሙ፡ ለ*ምዉታን፡ ወከመዝ፡ ተፈልጠ፡ ለመንፈሶሙ፡ ለጻድቃን፡ ዘውእቱ፡ ነቅዐ፡ ማይ፡ በላዕሌሁ፡ ብርህት።
source.note: Direct visual collation of the selected Charles1906 printed main text. Actual critical signs retained; only raised apparatus labels and printed verse labels suppressed. Punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial supplies and conjectures are not independent manuscript verification. V2: final selected word is actual four-glyph feminine adjective ብርህት, visually matched to the same printed form in22:2; v1 incorrectly transcribed the apparatus-reported noun from which it was emended. No other Geʽez bytes changed.

translation.text: He answered and said to me, “These three were made so that the spirits of the dead might be separated. In this way a place was set apart for the spirits of the righteous, where there is a spring of water, with brightness above it.[a]

footnotes.text: The actual selected numeral is three, despite four in22:2; it is not harmonized. A place is supplied in English with the impersonal separation clause. The final selected word ብርህት is the feminine adjective bright, visually identical to that in22:2. Charles printed58 note32 says it was emended from the noun ብርሃን with Greek φωτεινή; the source does not simply print the noun light. English brightness is a provisional nominalized rendering of this adjective, while above it retains the actual preposition and suffix. The suffix does not securely identify whether the spring, the place, or another antecedent is intended, and the relative/adjectival syntax remains uncertain; this is not a recovered clear predication. The editorial Greek-based choice is not independent manuscript attestation.

source.text: በከመ፡ ከማሁ፡ ተፈጥረ፡ ለኃጥኣን፡ ሶበ፡ ይመውቱ፡ ወይትቀበሩ፡ ውስተ፡ ምድር፡ ወኵነኔ፡ ኢኮነ፡ በላዕሌሆሙ፡ በሕይወቶሙ።
source.note: Direct visual collation of the selected Charles1906 printed main text. Actual critical signs retained; only raised apparatus labels and printed verse labels suppressed. Punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial supplies and conjectures are not independent manuscript verification.

translation.text: “In the same way a place was created for sinners when they die and are buried in the earth, and judgment had not come upon them during their life.

source.text: በዝየ፡ ይትፈለጠ፡ ነፍሳቲሆሙ፡ ዲበ፡ ዛቲ፡ ዐቢይ፡ ጻዕር፡ እስከ፡ አመ፡ ዐቢይ፡ ዕለት፡ እንተ፡ ኵነኔ፡ ወመቅሠፍት፡ ወጻዕር፡ ለእለ፡ ይረግሙ፡ እስከ፡ ለዓለም፡ ወበቀል፡ ለነፍሶሙ፡ በህየ፡ ይእስሮሙ፡ እስከ፡ ለዓለም፡ [ወእመኒ፡ ውእቱ፡ እምቅድመ፡ ዓለም።]
source.note: Direct visual collation of the selected Charles1906 printed main text. Actual critical signs retained; only raised apparatus labels and printed verse labels suppressed. Punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial supplies and conjectures are not independent manuscript verification.

translation.text: Here their souls are separated for this great torment until the great day of judgment, scourging, and torment for those who curse forever, and vengeance for their souls. There he will bind them forever [even though it is from before eternity].[a]

footnotes.text: The selected text has souls here; Charles printed58 note38 considers possible corruption to spirits, but the overlapping lexical uses do not justify replacing the actual word. Those who curse is the printed active form: Charles proposes a passive correction in printed58 note41/printed59 note9, but it is not installed here. The final bracketed clause is regarded as an Ethiopic intrusion by printed58 note44, and remains explicitly bracketed. The source does not name the subject of he will bind; English does not identify him. The time-clause grammar and shift into vengeance remain awkward rather than being harmonized.

source.text: ወከመዝ፡ ተፈልጠ፡ ለነፍሰ፡ እለ፡ ይስክዩ፡ እለ፡ ያርእዩ፡ በእንተ፡ ሕጉለት፡ አመ፡ ተቀትሉ፡ በመዋዕለ፡ ኃጥኣን።
source.note: Direct visual collation of the selected Charles1906 printed main text. Actual critical signs retained; only raised apparatus labels and printed verse labels suppressed. Punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial supplies and conjectures are not independent manuscript verification.

translation.text: “In this way a place was set apart for the souls of those who make accusation, who give testimony about their destruction when they were killed in the days of sinners.[a]

footnotes.text: A place is supplied with the impersonal was separated construction, as in22:9. The selected wording speaks of souls and accusation; the showing verb is rendered give testimony in the context of persons reporting their killing. It does not specify a philosophical definition of a soul or authorize changing the source noun to spirit. Their before destruction is contextual English, not an expressed possessive suffix.

source.text: ወከመዝ፡ ተፈጥረ፡ ለነፍሶሙ፡ ለሰብእ፡ እለ፡ ኢኮኑ፡ ጻድቃነ፡ አላ፡ ኃጥኣነ፡ እለ፡ ፍጹማነ፡ እበሳ፡ ወምስለ፡ አባሲያን፡ ይከውኑ፡ ከማሆሙ፡ ወነፍሶሙሰ፡ ኢትትቀተል፡ በዕለተ፡ ኵነኔ፡ ወኢ*ይትነሥኡ፡ *እምነ፡ ዝየ።
source.note: Direct visual collation of the selected Charles1906 printed main text. Actual critical signs retained; only raised apparatus labels and printed verse labels suppressed. Punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial supplies and conjectures are not independent manuscript verification. Full cross-page unit, printed58→60/PDF96→98, with PDF97 the facing Greek/apparatus. Initial ኢ in ኢትትቀተል is visually read as a negative, not OCR እ.

translation.text: “In this way a place was created for the souls of people who were not righteous but sinners, complete in wrongdoing, who will be with the wrongdoers, like them. But their soul will not be killed on the day of judgment, and they will not rise from here.”[a]

footnotes.text: The full selected unit continues onto printed60/PDF98. Both negatives are explicit: their soul will not be killed and they will not rise from here. The source shifts from a singular soul expression to a plural verb; English preserves that shift. Rise may also mean get up or be raised; the clause does not by itself settle a systematic doctrine of resurrection, soul immortality, or annihilation. No affirmative killing or rising is substituted.

source.text: ውእተ፡ ጊዜ፡ ባረክዎ፡ ለ*እግዚአ፡ ስብሐት፡ ወእቤ፡ ቡሩክ፡ እግዚአየ፡ እግዚአ፡ ጽድቅ፡ ዘይመልክ፡ እስከ፡ ለዓለም።
source.note: Direct visual collation of the selected Charles1906 printed main text. Actual critical signs retained; only raised apparatus labels and printed verse labels suppressed. Punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial supplies and conjectures are not independent manuscript verification.

translation.text: Then I blessed the Lord of Glory and said, “Blessed is my Lord, the Lord of Righteousness, who rules forever.”

source.text: ወእምህየ፡ ሖርኩ፡ ካልአ፡ መካነ፡ መንገለ፡ ዓረብ፡ እስከ፡ አጽናፈ፡ ምድር።
source.note: Direct visual collation of the selected Charles1906 printed main text. Actual critical signs retained; only raised apparatus labels and printed verse labels suppressed. Punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial supplies and conjectures are not independent manuscript verification.

translation.text: From there I went to another place toward the west, to the ends of the earth.

source.text: ወርኢኩ፡ እሳተ፡ ዘይነድድ፡ ዘይረውፅ፡ እንዘ፡ ኢ*ያዓርፍ፡ ወኢ*ይነትግ፡ እምሩፀቱ፡ መዐልተ፡ ወሌሊተ፡ አላ፡ ከማሁሙ።
source.note: Direct visual collation of the selected Charles1906 printed main text. Actual critical signs retained; only raised apparatus labels and printed verse labels suppressed. Punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial supplies and conjectures are not independent manuscript verification.

translation.text: I saw a burning fire that ran without resting or diminishing in its running, day and night, but continued in the same way.[a]

footnotes.text: Dillmann1865 cols660–661 gives decrease or diminish for ነተገ and explicitly cites Hen23:2. Both source negatives are retained. Continued is supplied to express the verbless final but in the same way; the selected form has a plural suffix, not a smoothly regular singular pronoun. Charles printed60 note10 questions whether burning is a gloss, but it remains in the selected main text.

source.text: ወተስእልኩ፡ እንዘ፡ እብል፡ ዝንቱ፡ ምንት፡ ውእቱ፡ ዘአልቦ፡ ዕረፍተ።
source.note: Direct visual collation of the selected Charles1906 printed main text. Actual critical signs retained; only raised apparatus labels and printed verse labels suppressed. Punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial supplies and conjectures are not independent manuscript verification.

translation.text: I asked, “What is this that has no rest?”

source.text: ውእተ፡ ጊዜ፡ አውሥአኒ፡ ራጉኤል፡ ፩እምነ፡ ቅዱሳን፡ መላእክት፡ ዘሀሎ፡ ምስሌየ፡ ወይቤለኒ፡ ዝንቱ፡ ዘርኢከ፡ ሩጸተ፡ †መዝኒ፡† መንገለ፡ ዐረብ፡ እሳት፡ ዘ*ይሰድድ፡ ውእቱ፡ ኵሎ፡ ብርሃናተ፡ ሰማይ።
source.note: Direct visual collation of the selected Charles1906 printed main text. Actual critical signs retained; only raised apparatus labels and printed verse labels suppressed. Punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial supplies and conjectures are not independent manuscript verification. The exact printed crux is †መዝኒ፡†, not OCR ተወዝኒ. English transliteration exposes an unresolved source-critical word instead of guessing its meaning.

translation.text: Then Raguel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered and said to me, “What you saw—the running †məzni† toward the west—is the fire that drives all the lights of heaven.”[a]

footnotes.text: The daggered English token məzni transliterates the actual daggered መዝኒ; its meaning in this clause remains unresolved. It is not a translated measured course. Charles printed60 note24 proposes alternatives involving the Greek or a corrupted Ethiopic form, but none is silently adopted. Dillmann1865 col211 has neighboring weighing, scales and a zodiacal name; that lexical proximity does not establish the precise sense of this daggered form here. The selected drives verb is itself an editorial emendation discussed in note25, and is retained without claiming independent manuscript verification.
